plan.title: KO vs WT drug response: 2x2 interaction DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question — does the drug act differently in knockout than in wild type — is a genotype x treatment interaction question on a balanced 2x2 design: 16 brain samples (metadata.csv, 16 x 4), 4 per cell (WT/vehicle, WT/drug, KO/vehicle, KO/drug), with raw salmon-derived integer gene-level counts for 12,000 gene symbols x 16 sample columns (counts.csv, 12000 x 17, first column = gene symbol). The design is fully crossed, balanced, and carries no declared batch, so a single DESeq2 negative-binomial fit with ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment answers the question directly: the interaction coefficient is the difference of differences (drug effect in KO minus drug effect in WT).

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC first (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to check that the four cells separate as expected and that no sample sits with the wrong group before any test is fit — the counts came from a quantifier, so a swapped label or a shallow library is the failure mode that would silently corrupt an interaction estimate. T1S2 fits the model and produces three result tables side by side: the drug effect in WT (reference cell), the drug effect in KO (main effect + interaction), and the interaction contrast itself. This triple is the answer; the interaction coefficient alone does not say whether the drug does anything in either genotype, and a simple effect alone does not say whether the genotypes differ. T1S2a repeats the interaction test with edgeR's quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and design as an independent-method robustness check, because at n=4 per cell the interaction estimate is the noisiest quantity in the design.

T2S1 takes the full ranked gene list per contrast into fgsea preranked GSEA against the human MSigDB hallmark collection and then GO BP, ranked on the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the disputed ranking choice is resolved in favour of the Wald statistic because it scales the effect by its uncertainty, which matters most for the low-powered interaction contrast. Ranked GSEA rather than over-representation is the right method here specifically because the interaction contrast is likely to yield few individually significant genes.

T1S3 assembles the report. Power is the honest limitation: with 4 replicates per cell the interaction coefficient has roughly double the standard error of a simple effect, so the expected outcome is far fewer significant interaction genes than significant treatment genes, and an empty interaction list is evidence of low power rather than evidence of no differential drug action. The report must state this explicitly rather than presenting the simple effects as if they answered the interaction question.

fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, per contrast, MSigDB Hallmark then GO BP
Interaction report: simple effects at both genotypes plus interaction contrast, MA and dispersion plots, reproducibility record

If a collection is absent at run time, report which one and continue with the collections that are present rather than substituting another organism
caveats: Enrichment results are method-dependent; present a significant set as a hypothesis for follow-up, not as a proven mechanism
GO BP is a nested hierarchy — parent and child sets share members, so expect correlated blocks of hits and collapse before counting findings

Ranking by the interaction statistic means a leading edge of genes whose drug response differs by genotype, not genes that respond to drug — this must be stated when the interaction table is interpreted

grounding.reason: Ranked GSEA on the full tested list, hallmark first then GO for human, once per contrast; the disputed ranking metric (R-0108) is resolved in favour of the Wald statistic because it scales the effect by its uncertainty, which matters most for the low-powered interaction contrast.

steps.name: Interaction report and synthesis
steps.question: Taken together, does the drug act differently in KO than in WT brain — and how strong is the evidence given 4 replicates per cell?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Present the three DESeq2 result sets side by side for the top genes: drug effect in WT (reference cell), drug effect in KO, and the interaction contrast, ranked by the ashr-shrunken log2 fold change, with unshrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE also shown. Name the reference levels (WT, vehicle) beside every table since every coefficient's meaning depends on them. Include the MA and dispersion plots and the p-value histograms from T1S2 before the gene tables, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S2a as the robustness statement, and the per-contrast hallmark and GO GSEA tables with leading-edge genes from T2S1. State the method, package versions, design formula, all three contrasts, the padj threshold, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes per contrast, the gene-set collection names and versions, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, the permutation seed, and sessionInfo. Close with an explicit power statement about the interaction test.
steps.context: The synthesis must answer the research question directly and calibrate the confidence. A 2x2 with n=4 has adequate power for main effects and poor power for the interaction; conflating the two is the main interpretive failure mode for this design.
acceptance_criteria: The three contrasts are presented side by side per gene, with reference levels named beside the tables
Report states the method, package versions, design formula, contrasts, thresholds, genes tested after filtering, and DE gene count per contrast
Enrichment reporting includes collection name and version, ranking metric, universe, size window, and leading-edge genes per significant set, with the method-dependence caveat stated
DESeq2 vs edgeR interaction overlap is reported as the robustness check, with the intersection labelled the high-confidence set

A closing paragraph states the power limitation of the interaction test at n=4 per cell explicitly, and states that an empty or short interaction list is consistent with low power rather than demonstrating that the drug acts identically in both genotypes
Reproducibility record included: sessionInfo, package versions, seed, gene-set collection versions
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep p-values from the unshrunken fit and name the shrinkage estimator (ashr) in the table header
Do not present a difference in significance status between the WT and KO simple effects as evidence of an interaction — only the interaction contrast supports that claim
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
State the size of the significant interaction gene list explicitly, however small
caveats: Interpretation of pathway hits from the interaction contrast differs from those of a simple effect and must be worded accordingly
No batch variable exists in the metadata; if T1S1 flagged unexplained structure in the PCA, note it as an uncontrolled source of variance rather than adjusting for it post hoc

grounding.reason: Interaction design report: simple effects and interaction contrast side by side with reference levels named, fit diagnostics, two-method overlap, enrichment provenance and the reproducibility record (R-0092, R-0042, R-0085, R-0087, R-0041, R-0051, R-0055, R-0105, R-0086).
